items.heading: 2. Keycloak (Security)
items.text: The `JUDO_PLATFORM_*` variables and the conversion rule above are read by the OSGi configuration mapper. The Guice runtime does not read Keycloak settings from environment variables: `JudoKeycloakModule` binds them from the `JudoKeycloakModuleConfiguration` object.

items.heading: 2. Keycloak (Security)
items.text: In the Guice runtime, `JudoKeycloakModule` binds the Keycloak server URL from `JudoKeycloakModuleConfiguration` (default `http://localhost:8080/auth`). The `KeycloakConnectorProvider` field default (`http://localhost:8080`) applies only when no server URL binding exists.

items.heading: 2. Keycloak (Security)
items.text: In the Guice runtime, the Keycloak admin password comes from `JudoKeycloakModuleConfiguration` (default `judo`). The `KeycloakConnectorProvider` field default (`admin`) applies only when no admin password binding exists.

items.heading: 1. Database (RDBMS)
items.text: The Guice PostgreSQL module stores a `poolSize` setting (default `10`) but does not apply it: `PostgresqlDataSourceProvider` wraps the driver in a `HikariDataSource` without setting a maximum pool size, so HikariCP's own default applies.

items.heading: ### Low-Level DAO and `QueryCustomizer`
items.text: The generated update call passes the access `QueryCustomizer` that the dispatcher builds for the caller into the DAO update. The runtime does not re-check derived-path membership after the write. Custom operations and direct DAO writes that do not pass such a customizer are not limited by the caller's membership filter, so enforce membership in the operation itself.

items.heading: Frontend guidance
items.text: Generated page files: `customization.ts` declares the custom-implementation interface keys and component interfaces for the container's visual elements, plus the container action hook key and hook type. `types.ts` declares the page action definitions and imports the data types the container uses. `src/config/layout.ts` is application-wide (drawer and divider sizes, theme and menu enums, the customization props), not per entity.

items.heading: Implementation Pattern
items.text: A DAO call from service code does not run them either: interceptors are attached to the dispatcher's built-in behaviours, and the DAO layer has no interceptor hook, so creating a child through the DAO skips the built-in create interceptor. Call the built-in operation through the dispatcher when its interceptor must run.

items.heading: Module Properties
items.text: Generator template parameters, including `debugPrint`, are set in the `<templateParameters>` element of the `judo-ui-generator-maven-plugin` `generate` configuration. The React template reads `debugPrint` from the template context (`ReactStoredVariableHelper.isDebugPrint`). That context value comes from the `templateVariables` step of `variablePrecedence` (default `projectProperties,templateVariables,propertiesFiles,environmentVariables,systemProperties`), which is the `<templateParameters>` map. No separate `<templateVariables>` element exists. When `debugPrint` is unset it is false.

items.heading: Platform base
items.text: A JCL script operation cannot raise a modeled fault and cannot call an OSGi service. The JCL grammar has no `throw` or fault statement and no service-reference form; its statements are declarations, calls, `return`, `unset`, `delete`, `new`, blocks, `if`, `for` and `while`. Put fault-raising logic and OSGi service calls in a Java custom implementation.

items.heading: Use the classification in the model and in code
items.text: `<Enum>.getByOrdinal(ordinal)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` with the message `Invalid ordinal: <n>` for an ordinal that matches no member, and for `null`. The generated DTO mapping calls it when it converts an ordinal to an enumeration value, so an out-of-range ordinal fails there.

items.heading: Resolution order (`DefaultActorResolver`)
items.text: The actor lookup runs after the `authenticate` hooks and before the operation body. A first call from a new user, with no actor row yet, fails with `AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND` unless an `AuthenticationInterceptor.authenticate` hook has already created the row; a row created in `success` or in the operation body is too late for that request.
